Auth.//: Windows (Negotiate, for IIS) or Dev (signs everyone in without a password, with DevAuth:Roles). Production refuses to start unless this is Windows.

RoleMapping.//: Seeds the AD group to role mappings on first run only; after that they're edited in Administration. Role names: Analyst, ActionOwner, Reader, Admin. Groups as DOMAIN\Group, Group (this server's domain) or a SID.

Database.//: Sqlite (development) or SqlServer (production). ApplyMigrations=false when a DBA applies the schema script and the app pool has no db_owner.

DataProtection.//: An absolute folder for the key ring (antiforgery and circuit state), so sign-ins survive an app-pool recycle. Blank in development.

Files.//: Screenshots and files are kept on disk here, outside the web root in production. MaxImageMB caps one image; MaxEvidenceMB caps any other file on an action or its comments. Whether an action's files download in a password-protected zip is set in the app (Administration > Teams & SLA).

Org.//: The organization's time zone (IANA id), when the daily brief meets, and the team name on slides. The defaults: an administrator sets them in the app (Administration > Organization > Organization settings), and a value saved there wins.

Distribution.//: Defaults for the edition ceilings; an administrator can change them in the app. The public (company-wide) edition carries nothing above PublicMaxTlp; the team edition and the meeting nothing above TeamMaxTlp.
Distribution.//Recipients: Who each edition is emailed to until an administrator sets the lists in the app (Access & distribution).
Distribution.//RequireSharePoint: Whether a brief isn't finished until someone confirms its SharePoint copy was posted. Off by default; an administrator can turn it on in the app.

Email.//: Sending the brief through the organization's SMTP relay. Enabled=false sends nothing. EnableSsl uses STARTTLS. Sign in with SmtpUsername and SmtpPassword (set the password as the Email__SmtpPassword environment variable, not here) or SmtpUseDefaultCredentials (the app-pool account), or neither. PickupDirectory (development) writes .eml files there instead of sending.

Sla.//: Default business days a new action gets before it's due, by priority, and by kind where that should win (e.g. "IocSweep": 1). Administrators can change them in the app (Teams & SLA).

Notifications.//: Reminder and digest emails, each off until enabled; each goes once. These are the defaults: an administrator sets them in the app (Administration > Organization > Teams & SLA), and a value saved there wins. Times are in Org:TimeZone. DueSoon and Overdue go at ReminderTime on business days, as does Presenting (to whoever presents the brief the next business day); Digest weekly per team on Digest:Day at Digest:Time; BriefNotReady nudges the presenting analyst (or BriefNotReady:Recipients when there's no brief) at its Time if today's brief isn't ready.

Intake.//: Polling the sources (Administration > Sources). Off until Enabled; an administrator can still poll one by hand. Enabled, MinPollMinutes (the shortest poll interval) and RetentionDays (how many days feed items nobody kept are retained; an item published longer ago than that isn't taken in) are defaults an administrator sets in the app on Sources, as are SkipSponsored (a feed item that reads as sponsored isn't taken in, and counts as filtered out), SponsoredMarkers (the phrases that mark one, separated by semicolons, matched as whole words ignoring case in an item's author, source, tags, title and the start of its summary) and SponsoredExceptions (phrases that contain a marker but aren't sponsorship, such as state-sponsored). Set here only: Proxy (read at startup) for outbound requests, and a time and size limit per request. AllowPrivateNetworks lets feeds and CVE mirrors on private addresses (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, IPv6 unique-local) be fetched; loopback and link-local addresses never are. ReadingDays (1 to 30) is how long an article read in triage's reading pane is kept, for colleagues and the editor to reuse; it's never sent or exported. ReadSeconds (2 to 60) is how long reading an article's page may take, in triage or for the editor, before it's refused; an administrator raises it on Sources for a slow server. PullNowMinutes (1 to 1440) is the analyst pull-now window: a source pulled within it, on schedule or by hand, can't be pulled again from Triage's Sources tab until it's passed (an administrator's Poll now on Sources isn't held to it); an administrator sets it on Sources.
Intake.SponsoredMarkers: Sponsored; Sponsored by; Sponsored content; Sponsored post; Partner content; Paid post; Paid content; Advertorial

Import.//: Reading the opening metrics' values from CSV files (Administration > Metric imports, where an administrator sets DropFolderEnabled and PollMinutes in the app; these are the defaults). With DropFolderEnabled, files left in metrics-inbox under Files:RootPath are imported every PollMinutes and moved to its processed or rejected folder. Administrators can upload a file either way.

Ai.//: AI drafting help in the article editor (ADR 0004). Off until Provider is set (AzureOpenAI, with the resource's Endpoint and the model Deployment); set the key as the Ai__ApiKey environment variable, never here. Nothing above MaxTlp is ever sent. WebGrounding lets Azure's web search (Grounding with Bing: billed separately, outside the Azure data boundary) look up an article TIDE can't fetch, for sources marked Open and TLP:CLEAR articles only. With no provider, analysts can still copy a prompt to run in an approved tool.

Cve.//: CVE enrichment from CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS and NVD for the CVEs on articles and recent feed items. Off until Enabled; Enabled and RefreshHours are defaults an administrator sets in the app (Administration > Sources). Set an NVD API key as the Cve__NvdApiKey environment variable for faster NVD lookups. The URLs can point at an internal mirror.

Updates.//: Checking GitHub for newer TIDE releases (Administration > System > Updates): one anonymous request every CheckIntervalHours (6 to 168), through Intake:Proxy when set. Off until CheckEnabled. Both are defaults an administrator sets in the app; Repository is set here only.

App.//: The address readers reach TIDE at (https://tide.example.org), for the 'Open in TIDE' link in email. Blank leaves the link out.
App.//PathBase: Only behind a reverse proxy that forwards a sub-path (such as /tide). Under IIS, as an application within another site, IIS sets it and this stays blank.
